title: Activation Capacity Heatmap + Sprintboard (Adaptive Batching rollout)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc maps capacity needs and KPIs for the Adaptive Batching + KV-cache pilot rollout. Goal is to get a safe 8-week canary -> staged rollout that keeps P95 latency under 300ms for web tier customers while reducing token cost by >=12% vs baseline.

Scope:
- Feature: Adaptive batching runtime (v1.2) + KV prefix-cache enabled for text-generation endpoints.
- Environments: canary (10% traffic), staged (50%), GA (100%).
- Customers: internal beta cohort (5 customers), self-serve web apps only for initial rollout. Dedicated & Private excluded from phase 1.

Executive goals (measurable):
- User-visible: P95 latency <= 300ms (web requests) AND 99.9% availability during rollout window.
- Cost: average token compute cost reduction >=12% for gen endpoints within 4 weeks of rollout.
- Quality: model output regression <= 1.0% on squad of 250 golden prompts (automated eval).
- Operational: cache hit rate >= 22% for eligible requests by week 3.

Baseline (last 30d):
- P50/P95 latency: 85ms / 410ms
- 99th percentile error rate: 0.15%
- Avg token cost (hosted): $0.018 per 1k tokens
- Cache hit rate (manual test): 0-3% (not enabled in prod)

Week-by-week sprintboard (8 weeks)
W0 (pre-canary):
- Finalize canary cohort + customer opt-ins (Owner: Priya).
- Smoke tests and infra capacity reservation (Owner: Evan).
- QA golden prompts and eval harness locked (Owner: Tomás).
- Communication: internal beta invite email template + docs (Owner: Aisha).
W1 (canary 10%):
- Deploy AB runtime to canary pool; KV-cache enabled but write-through disabled.
- Run 24h high-traffic soak at 10%: collect latency + error signals.
- Manual review of first 2 days of eval diffs.
W2 (canary 10% -> 25% if healthy):
- If quality and SLOs met, ramp to 25% and enable aggressive batching rules for longer sequences.
- Observe cache hit rate and token-cost delta.
W3 (staged 50% gate prep):
- Capacity stress test: simulate 1.5x expected peak with autoscaler disabled to observe queuing characteristics.
- Lock rollback window and escalation owners.
W4 (50% staged):
- Promote to 50% with 2h hold periods between increments (25% -> 50% chunked).
- Run battlecard and incident drills with SRE on-call.
W5 (observe):
- Hold and measure 7-day rolling signals, begin GA readiness review.
W6 (final controls):
- Finalize traffic split automation and routing fallback to baseline model variant.
W7 (GA soft-launch 100% internal):
- Full production traffic for internal traffic only (no external customers).
W8 (GA external):
- Open to self-serve customers, monitor first 48h intensive.

Readiness checklist (quick)
- [ ] Canaries identified + customer opt-in confirmed
- [ ] Autoscaler behavior documented and verified under load
- [ ] Tracing hooks in place (per-request token-level timings)
- [ ] Golden prompt regression < 1.0% across all canary runs
- [ ] Rollback play defined and smoke-tested (see runbook)
- [ ] Billing/usage-metering snapshot for trend comparison captured
- [ ] Communication templates (status page, support KB, customer FAQs) ready

Capacity heatmap (plan and quick sim)
Notes: use hourly heatmap for first 7 days after each promotion. Key dims: expected QPS, GPU slot saturation, batching multiplier effect, KV-cache hit rate.
Pseudo-table (hourly expected)
- Normal baseline peak QPS: 1400 reqs/hr
- Expected web burst (10x spiky): 14,000 reqs/hr for 15-30 minutes
- Target buffer: autoscaler to cover 2x baseline within 5m

Simple estimator (for crude checks):
- Effective throughput = raw_qps * (1 + batching_gain + cache_hit_reduction)
- batching_gain estimate: 0.18 (i.e., 18% token-cost reduction from batching)
- cache_hit_reduction: cache_hit_rate * 0.35 (cache bypass still necessary sometimes)
Example: 1400 * (1 - (0.18 + 0.22*0.35)) ~= 1400 * (1 - 0.257) ~= 1043 effective ops -> maps to N GPU slots via perf table in infra PR.

Surge scenarios + thresholds
- Signal A: P95 > 350ms for > 10m -> action: pause further rollout increments; notify SRE and product-ops.
- Signal B: error rate > 0.5% and rising -> action: immediate rollback to last good model variant, page on-call.
- Signal C: cache hit rate falls below 8% for 24h -> action: investigate prefix mismatch rules, slow-evaluate and disable cache for affected routes if needed.

Rollout policy (canary rules)
- Promotion criteria from canary -> staged:
  1) P95 within 300ms for last 12h average
  2) Golden prompt regression <= 1.0% daily
  3) Error rate < 0.2% 24h rolling
- Automated rollback triggers include: P95 spike > 25% vs baseline for 15m, or error rate > 0.5% 10m window.

Observability (dashboards & alerts)
- Dashboards to glue: per-route latency (p50/p95/p99), token-cost per request, KV-cache hit rate, batching size distribution, model-eval diffs.
- Key alert thresholds (pager):
  - P95 latency above 350ms sustained 10m -> page SRE
  - Error rate above 0.5% sustained 5m -> page SRE + product-ops
  - Regression fail on golden suite (daily) -> notify ML lead and product-ops

Communication plan
- Internal: #prodops-launch Slack channel -> auto-post canary health every 15m during ramp windows. Standup sync at 09:30 PT daily for first week of promotion.
- External customers: one-off email to beta cohort with rollback assurances + link to support KB. Post-GA: staged release notes on docs.

Runbook excerpt (immediate rollback)
1) Identify root traffic tag (canary id).
2) Use traffic switcher to redirect canary -> baseline model variant (route id: gen-web-v1).
3) Disable adaptive batching config via runtime flags (flags: batching.enabled=false).
4) Re-evaluate ingest logs for 10m, confirm P95 back to baseline.
5) Post-mortem to follow within 72h; owner: Aisha.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self)
- Confirm cost-modeling for reserved dedicated capacity vs hosted during ramp (Finance contact: Emma K.).
- Add load pattern for EU region (currently US-weighted sim).
- Decide whether to enable write-through cache for private customers in phase 2.

Post-launch evaluation (KPI windows)
- 24h: immediate SLO check and incident triage if any alerts fired.
- 7d: cost delta calc across cohort and whole-traffic sample.
- 30d: elasticity review and ops playbook adjustments; decide on GA backfill for dedicated/private.

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Eval harness: /repos/evals/adaptive-batching/runbook.md (see linked PR)
- Capacity perf table (infra): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/blob/main/capacity-table.md
- Related playbooks: Confluence link (top of doc).

Notes: this is a working doc — expect edits after the first canary day. Use checklist as source of truth for launch readiness sign-off.

Owners & signoffs (pre-GA):
- Product-ops lead: Aisha Patel (owner)
- ML lead: Tomás Rivera
- SRE lead: Evan Chen
